title: Page-aware fused-attn reservoir scheduler
content:
Context and motivation:

We continue to see tail-latency spikes for long-context decode workloads when paged-KV is active and we attempt to use aggressive FlashAttention + fused ops kernels. Root cause summary from recent traces: page thrashing (hot working set crosses page boundary), bursty concurrent requests causing contention on DMA lanes, and kernel launch jitter when pages are migrated in the middle of an attention window. Existing prefetch heuristics are reactive and treat candidate pages independently; they overfetch during multi-tenant bursts and underfetch when access locality shifts slowly.

Goal of this doc:
- Sketch a lightweight scheduling primitive (reservoir scheduler) that prioritizes page prefetches and fused-attn launches by combining recency/score with a bounded reservoir to avoid overcommit.
- Define kernel-level residency hints so fused-attn kernels can make safe tradeoffs (speculative KV use vs. conservative fallbacks).
- Design telemetry counters and experiment plan to validate latency/cost tradeoffs.

Key ideas (high level):
1) Reservoir for page prefetching: maintain a small probabilistic buffer (reservoir) of page candidates per GPU-stream-class that is updated per request with weighted sampling rather than strict top-k. This reduces synchronized bursts where many requests all enqueue the same top pages and cause DMA saturation. The reservoir size is tuned to keep DMA concurrency within a target (e.g., 2x lanes).

2) Per-request page-score that includes:
- prefix-match score (how many prefix tokens would need that page)
- recency (LRU decayed)
- cross-request cohort score (if other inflight requests likely need the same page)
- kernel-fit penalty (is this page layout aligned for fused-attn kernel fast path?)
Combine these into a single numeric priority used by the reservoir sampler.

3) Kernel residency hints (lightweight struct passed in launch params):
- RESIDENCY_CONFIDENT (page is resident and pinned) => allow FlashAttention fused path that assumes no page-migration mid-window and uses aggressive prefetching into shared memory/registers.
- RESIDENCY_PROBABLE (page expected to arrive soon) => fused path can speculatively launch but must include a small safe-check (fast path vs. slow path switch) — see below.
- RESIDENCY_UNSURE (not resident) => use conservative fused kernel or fallback to non-fused kernel to avoid mid-kernel remote-mem accesses.

Note: the hint is advisory only; runtime decision still checks page pin state atomically at launch. Hints used to order reservoir priorities and to choose kernel variants.

4) Speculative fused kernel micro-probe: A short (microseconds) check at beginning of kernel to verify page residency for the working slice; if failed, the kernel signals and exits fast (no heavy work), and the request requeues to a conservative path. Mechanism: kernel reads a small residency bitmap in L1 (populated by prefetch controller via environment-buffered marker); if any miss, it performs a safe early return code path. This keeps worst-case wasted cycles bounded.

5) Page reshuffle/backoff policy: If reservoir sampling sees repeated misses for pages in the reservoir, adapt by reshuffling weights toward recent smaller ranges and reduce prefetch TTL. This prevents repeated re-fetch of cold pages when access patterns drift.

Scheduling algorithm (sketch):
- On request arrival, compute candidate page list from token ranges and map to page-score vector.
- Insert candidates into reservoir for the stream-class with weighted sampling (weights = exp(alpha * score)). Reservoir capacity R tuned by lane count and average DMA latency.
- Reservoir eviction uses stochastic replacement to keep diversity across requests.
- Prefetch worker dequeues reservoir entries up to DMA concurrency budget and issues page pulls. It annotates page metadata with last-request-id and confidence.
- Kernel orchestrator consults page metadata and the kernel residency hint to choose fused vs conservative kernel. If fused chosen, kernel receives micro-probe bitmap.

Kernel changes (implementation notes):
- Create small residency bitmap per page-group (64B per group) maintained by host-side prefetch controller; updated atomically when page pinned/unpinned. Place the bitmap address in device-visible constant memory for micro-probe latency.
- Add a 2-path fused-attn kernel variant: fast_path that assumes residency, and a guarded entry that performs the micro-probe and jumps to slow_path on miss. Keep codegen footprint minimal to avoid register pressure.
- Provide an API for kernel launch flags: residency_hint (enum), probe_mask_ptr, and a reservation_token id to correlate with telemetry.

Telemetry and metrics to gather:
- per-request latency broken down by: prefetch wait, kernel micro-probe time, fused-fast-path vs fallback counts, DMA queue depth over time, and page-hit ratio for first window token.
- tail-percentiles (p50,p95,p99,p999) before/after enabling reservoir scheduler.
- kernel occupancy and SM efficiency for both fast and fallback kernels (to detect register-pressure regressions).
- cost delta (extra DMA bandwidth) vs latency saved (tokens/ms).

Experiment plan (short):
1) Microbench on single-GPU with synthetic trace: sliding-window access with controlled drift to test reshuffle behavior. Metric: number of re-fetches per request and mean latency.
2) Multi-tenant test with 10 concurrent small-batch clients to validate reservoir reduces DMA spikes. Metric: DMA lane saturation events and p99 latency.
3) End-to-end Redwood infer harness with full LLM model (16k context) compare: baseline (current prefetch), reservoir-only, reservoir+speculative-fused. Measure token throughput and tail-latency.

Open design issues / questions:
- How to select reservoir size R automatically per-GPU? Candidate approach: sample short warmup and measure DMA-latency distribution; set R = clip(k * median-RTT / mean-kernel-duration).
- Micro-probe tradeoff: how long can micro-probe be (in cycles) before it becomes counterproductive? We need microbench numbers.
- Consistency semantics around page pin/unpin races: we rely on host atomic flips of bitmap and kernel seeing a transient false-positive; must ensure correctness (no silent corruption).
- How to integrate with existing kv-eviction policies (LRU/hybrid)? The reservoir should send signals to the eviction layer to hold pages for high-cohort locality.

Immediate TODOs:
- (Maya) implement residency bitmap proto and device constant pointer plumbing in runtime (PR stub: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2467).
- (Ravi) microbench for micro-probe loop to measure safe probe amortization.
- (Elena) simulate reservoir sampler on trace logs from last 2 weeks to estimate ideal R and alpha.
- Add unit tests: eviction signals, kernel fallback correctness, and telemetry labeling for reservation_token.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and incremental: we prefer adding an early-exit micro-probe and an admission reservoir rather than full predictive ML prefetching. The scheduler should reduce worst-case bursts without significantly increasing average DMA usage.
- Look for places where the bitmap address leaks or increases kernel constant memory pressure — that is the most likely performance regression risk.

References and related context:
- See existing KV prefetch controller prototype notes (ref: SRV-1024) and flashattn fused path work in earlier PRs. This doc attempts to complement those sketches by focusing on probabilistic admission and a bounded speculative kernel strategy.

Last thoughts: reservoir admission + guarded fused kernel gives a simple mechanism to reduce synchronized overfetch and bound wasted work when pages miss. If microbench results are promising, follow-up: adaptive R tuning and a light-weight per-tenant QoS knob to bias reservoir behavior.
